summary: Interim: no confirmed unauthorized access so far. All SSH logins on web-01, db-01 and ci-01 match the staff directory (known keys and home/office addresses), the CI key from 10.20.0.30, and db-01's backup key. Password logins to deploy come from Maria's addresses and from 54.36.199.108. That address checks in every few hours with a sub-second, never-failing command and never uses sudo, which fits the "old monitoring box" that holds the deploy password, so I'm not treating it as an intruder. Maria: please confirm that 54.36.199.108 is the monitoring box. There is heavy brute-forcing of deploy/jpark from the internet, with no successes. Fixes on web-01: locked jpark (not in the staff directory, had a password and full sudo; also locked on ci-01); removed deploy's NOPASSWD sudo for rsync (a path to root that the release doesn't use); quarantined the old "Blue Ridge Web Co." must-use plugin, whose ?asup= endpoint answered without a login and leaked database details; changed the larkspur-orders root cron so it no longer runs PHP code from wp-config.php (writable by deploy/www-data) as root or evals its output; and fixed a symlink/chown privilege escalation in larkspur-mailing-export. Release, payouts, orders, report and exports were all tested and still work.

Final: I found no sign that anyone without authorization got into an account or server. All successful SSH logins on web-01, db-01 and ci-01 match the staff directory (their usual keys and home/office addresses), the CI key from ci-01, and db-01's backup key. Password logins to the shared deploy account come only from Maria's addresses and from 54.36.199.108. That address has checked in every 2–6 hours for the whole 14 days with a command lasting a few milliseconds; it never failed a login, never used sudo and changed no files (I watched the 16:20 session). That matches the "old monitoring box" that rotate-secret lists as holding the deploy password, so I did not block it or rotate any secrets; nothing shows a secret was read. Maria: please confirm 54.36.199.108 is that box. The internet noise is only noise: SSH brute force against deploy, jpark and mreyes, and revslider/Grafana path-traversal probes, all failed.

Weaknesses fixed (I tested each change and the shop still works):
web-01:
1) Locked jpark (not in the staff directory, had a password and full NOPASSWD sudo, being brute-forced); also locked on ci-01.
2) Removed deploy's NOPASSWD sudo for /usr/bin/rsync, an easy path to root that the release doesn't use. larkspur-deploy and larkspur-restart are unchanged.
3) Moved the old "Blue Ridge Web Co." must-use plugin to /root/quarantine. Its ?asup= endpoint answered without a login, leaked the database host, name and user, and could delete cache files.
4) larkspur-orders (root cron) ran PHP code from wp-config.php, which deploy and www-data can modify, as root and eval'd its output; that was a path from the web user to root. It now reads the file as www-data, without eval.
5) larkspur-mailing-export wrote and chowned files as root in the user's home, so a planted symlink could take over any file. It now builds the CSV in a root-only temp folder and writes it as the user.
ci-01:
6) The repo config holding the GitHub token was world-readable; it is now 660 root:developers.
7) The root maintenance job ran git gc on a repo whose hooks and config the developers group can write, which let any developer become root. Git now runs as deploy; I updated web-01's internal copy of the script to match.

Checked after the changes: release ok every 3 min (883881f), dumps reach ci-01 (16:20), payouts ok, orders and report ok, exports work.

Left for Maria: SSH password login is still on for staff who use passwords; consider moving them to keys. Forminator 1.25.0 is outdated; update it. The deploy password is still shared with the monitoring box; give that box a key with a from= restriction. offsite-backup fails only because there's no internet access.

Final (updated 16:25): I found no sign that anyone without authorization got into an account or server, so I rotated no secrets. All successful SSH logins on the three servers match the staff directory (known keys, home/office addresses), CI's key from ci-01, or db-01's backup key. tbrooks logged in at 16:23 from a new address, 67.180.176.27, with his usual laptop key; I consider that legitimate. Password logins to deploy come from Maria's addresses and from 54.36.199.108. That address has checked in every 2–6 hours for all 14 days with a session of a few milliseconds; it never failed a login, never used sudo and changed no files (I watched the 16:20 session). That matches the "old monitoring box" that holds the deploy password, so I left it alone. Maria: please confirm it is that box. Only Maria and Lucia logged in to WordPress, and only dana to Grafana. The rest is internet noise: SSH password guessing and revslider/Grafana path-traversal probes, all failed.

Fixes (each tested; release every 3 min, dumps to ci-01, payouts, settle, orders, report and exports are all OK at 16:24):
web-01:
1) Locked the jpark Unix account (not in the staff directory; password + full sudo; being brute-forced), also on ci-01. Removed jpark's (jun@parkdev.io) WordPress administrator role; the account and content are kept and its sessions destroyed.
2) Removed deploy's NOPASSWD sudo for rsync (a path to root the release doesn't use).
3) Moved the old "Blue Ridge Web Co." must-use plugin to /root/quarantine (its ?asup= endpoint answered without a login and leaked database details).
4) larkspur-orders (root cron) no longer runs code from wp-config.php as root or evals its output; it reads the file as www-data.
5) larkspur-mailing-export no longer writes/chowns as root in the user's home (symlink privilege escalation).
6) The CI key in deploy's authorized_keys now works only from ci-01 (from="10.20.0.30"); the 16:24 release confirmed it still works.
ci-01:
7) The repo config with the GitHub token was world-readable; now 660 root:developers.
8) The root maintenance job's git gc on a developer-writable repo (any developer → root) now runs as deploy; web-01's internal copy of the script was updated to match.
Originals of the changed files are in /root/quarantine on web-01 and /root/ci-01.sh.orig on ci-01.

Recommendations: move staff off SSH passwords to keys; update Forminator 1.25.0; give the monitoring box its own key with a from= restriction instead of the shared deploy password; remove Maria's unused "work-laptop-old" key (all her logins use the MacBook key); the node exporter on port 9100 is reachable from the internet (counters only; I left it because I don't know who scrapes it). offsite-backup on web-01 fails only because there is no internet access.

All successful SSH logins on the three servers match the staff directory (each person's known key or password, from home/office/mobile addresses), CI's key from ci-01, or db-01's backup key. Some staff logged in from new home addresses with their usual keys (tbrooks 67.180.176.27 and 73.162.151.199, nvega 50.39.125.166); their sessions were normal. Password logins to deploy came only from Maria's address ranges (73.162.x, 100.37.x, 96.255.6.208) and from 54.36.199.108. That address has checked in every 2–6 hours for 14 days, and twice today (16:20 and 16:25, perhaps re-checking after the host move). Each session ran one command lasting a few milliseconds, with no sudo, no processes left and no files changed. That matches the "old monitoring box" that holds the deploy password, so I left it alone. Maria: please confirm it is that box. Only Maria and Lucia logged in to WordPress and only dana to Grafana. SSH password guessing and revslider/Grafana path-traversal probes all failed.
